title: In how many ways can A be joined to make a right angle?
description: On the same two dot grids, the line AB is extended past A to make a straight angle, and a line through A that splits it into two equal parts is the one that makes a right angle. The dots on that line are counted in each grid, and a corner of folded paper is the check.
teaching_notes: One idea: a right angle at A needs a line through A that splits the straight angle into two equal parts, and every grid dot on it counts, on both sides of A. Watch for students who count the dots on one side only.

video_script.why: The child finds all the dots that make a right angle with a given line by splitting the straight angle into two equal parts.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two dot grids, each with A and B joined
video_script.anchor: two dot grids, seven columns by six rows, each with A and B joined
video_script.payoff_line: The left grid has five ways, and the right grid has four ways

final_answer.value: left grid 5 ways, right grid 4 ways; the new segment must be at right angles to AB through A
final_answer.spoken: the left grid has five ways, and the right grid has four ways, because the new line must be at right angles to the line of eigh bee

maths_rules: two grids of 7 columns by 6 rows; extend BA past A to C; a right angle at A needs a line through A that splits the straight angle CAB into two equal parts
left grid: A at row 3, column 4; AB is horizontal, so the perpendicular is upright through A: 2 dots above (rows 1 and 2) and 3 dots below (rows 4, 5 and 6), 5 ways

right grid: A at row 3, column 3; AB goes 1 across and 1 down per step, so the perpendicular goes 1 across and 1 up, or 1 back and 1 down: dots at row 2 column 4, row 1 column 5, row 4 column 2, row 5 column 1, 4 ways
check: the corner of a folded paper, a right angle, fits at A with one arm along AB and the other arm through these dots
video_script.design: One idea: the line through A that splits the straight angle into two equal parts, and all the grid dots on it. The two grids stay on the board.
open_questions: The positions of A and B in the two grids follow the worklist's description of the book's figures; the figures could not be viewed, so the counts five and four are not checked against the pictures.
